page: Amazon Web Services c8g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the ARM64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs utilizing the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and a 36 MB L3 cache. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in memory bandwidth for large blocks, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core and text processing metrics, all scoring in the top 25%. Most other compute and memory metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core performance, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, fall within the middle 50% average. However, the instance exhibits performance limitations in specific areas, showing weak results in the Passmark CPU encryption test and poor performance in prompt processing for medium-sized 7B LLM models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8g.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile for ARM-native applications, delivering dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading overhead. This makes it suitable for compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and lightweight single-threaded decompression tasks. It is less suited for cryptographic-heavy operations or medium-to-large language model inference due to hardware-level performance tradeoffs.
